## Digital Marketing Agency in Pune: What Meta Removing Placement Exclusions Means for Your Ad Spend in 2026

Around 25 August 2026, advertisers running Meta campaigns started noticing something small on their screen but big in its consequences: the checkboxes that let you exclude specific placements — Facebook Audience Network, Reels, Stories, Instagram Explore — at the ad-set level had simply vanished from Ads Manager. If you run Meta campaigns for a Pune business or an NGO, or you are evaluating a digital marketing agency in Pune to manage that spend, this matters because it quietly converts a hard "never show my ad here" rule into a soft "make it expensive to show my ad here" rule. The difference sounds technical. It is not — it is the difference between a brand-safety control that actually blocks a placement and one that merely makes that placement a little less likely to win, while your budget can still land there.

This article walks through what changed, why it fits a longer pattern of Meta narrowing manual control over the past 18 months, and — most usefully — exactly how to set up the one control that still works: an account-level exclusion in Brand Safety & Suitability. We also cover what a competent digital marketing agency in Pune should be auditing in every client account this quarter, because this change went out quietly, without an official Meta announcement, and plenty of ad accounts are running on exclusions that no longer do what their owners think they do.

## What Actually Changed at the Ad-Set Level

Until late August 2026, an advertiser building an ad set in Meta Ads Manager could open the Placements section, choose "Manual placements," and uncheck the ones they didn't want — say, Audience Network for a client worried about clickbait content sitting next to their brand, or Instagram Explore for a lead-generation campaign for a Pune-based [B2B service business](/services/lead-generation) that wanted stricter placement discipline. That checkbox is what disappeared. Multiple ad-tech publications documented advertisers losing the option entirely, not through a rollout notice from Meta but through advertiser reports and screenshots comparing accounts before and after.

In place of the checkbox, Meta pushed advertisers toward its "value rules" mechanism. Value rules let you apply a bid adjustment to a placement, a device type, or an audience segment — ranging from as generous as +1000% (bid far more aggressively for a placement you like) down to as punishing as -90% (bid far less for one you don't). A -90% adjustment on Audience Network, for instance, makes Meta's auction system extremely reluctant to spend there, since your bid is now competing at a fraction of its normal strength. But "extremely reluctant" is not "never." A -90% discount is still a live, spendable bid — in a low-competition auction, or when Meta's delivery system decides that placement is the only inventory available to hit your target, spend can still land there.

### Why a Discount Is Not a Block

This is the part that gets lost in the headline. A hard exclusion removes a placement from the auction entirely for that ad set — zero possibility of delivery. A -90% value rule leaves the placement in the auction with a heavily discounted bid — a small but real possibility of delivery. For most advertisers optimizing purely for cost-per-result, that distinction barely registers; a placement that wins auctions at a 90% discount is probably cheap and fine. But for advertisers who excluded a placement for brand-safety or compliance reasons — not cost reasons — the distinction is the entire point of the setting. If your NGO client cannot risk a donation appeal appearing next to certain third-party content on Audience Network, "90% less likely" is not the same commitment as "will not happen," and treating it as equivalent is where accounts get into trouble.

## This Is Not a One-Off — It's a Pattern Going Back to January 2025

The August 2026 change did not happen in isolation. It is the fourth step in a documented, multi-year sequence of Meta narrowing manual targeting and placement control, and any digital marketing agency in Pune managing Meta budgets should be tracking this sequence rather than reacting to each step as a surprise.

### 21 January 2025 — Detailed Targeting Exclusions Removed

Meta removed the ability to exclude detailed targeting segments (interests, behaviors) from campaigns, pushing advertisers toward broader, algorithm-driven audience definitions instead of manually carving out who should not see an ad.

### 16 October 2025 — The 5% "Leak" Introduced to Placement Exclusions

Meta began defaulting a small slice of budget — around 5% — to placements an advertiser had marked as excluded. In other words, even before the checkbox disappeared entirely, an "excluded" placement was already not a guaranteed zero. This is the detail advertisers most commonly missed, because the setting still looked identical in the interface; the enforcement behind it had quietly changed.

### 18 February 2026 — Advantage+ Unification Bans Campaign-Level Exclusions

Meta merged its manual and Advantage+ campaign structures into a single unified flow, making automated placement and audience decisions the default path for most new campaigns and prohibiting campaign-level placement exclusions outright under that structure. We covered the mechanics and lead-generation implications of this shift in detail in [our earlier piece on Meta's Advantage+ merge](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-meta-advantage-plus-leads-2026) — it is worth reading alongside this article because the two changes compound each other: campaign-level exclusion was gone by February, and now ad-set-level exclusion is gone too.

### ~25 August 2026 — Ad-Set-Level Exclusion Checkboxes Removed Entirely

The subject of this article: the last remaining manual placement-exclusion surface, at the ad set, replaced by the value-rule bid-adjustment mechanism described above.

Laid out chronologically, the pattern is unambiguous — Meta has removed manual exclusion controls at every level (targeting, campaign, ad set) over roughly 19 months, each time replacing a hard rule with a softer, bid-based or algorithm-driven substitute. None of these four changes were framed by Meta as "we are removing your ability to say no" — each was framed as a simplification or a unification. The practical effect for advertisers has been the same each time: less certainty that "excluded" means excluded.

## The Real Risk: Silent Budget Leakage on "Blocked" Placements

Put plainly, if your ad account has ad-set-level placement exclusions that were built before August 2026 — perhaps set up by a previous vendor, an in-house team member, or an earlier engagement with a [digital marketing agency in Pune](/services/meta-ads) — those exclusions have not been deleted from your ad sets. They have been converted, silently and without your input, into value rules with a steep bid discount. Nobody told you. The setting still shows something in the interface. But the guarantee behind it changed.

For most performance-driven campaigns, this converts into modest, forgivable budget drift — a percentage point or two of spend landing somewhere slightly less efficient. For campaigns where the exclusion existed for brand-safety, client-contract, or reputational reasons rather than cost reasons, this is a materially different risk. A financial-services client, a healthcare-adjacent client, or an NGO with donor-facing compliance requirements may have specifically instructed their agency: "our ads must never appear on Audience Network" or "keep us off Reels for regulatory reasons." If that instruction was implemented as an ad-set-level exclusion any time before this year, it is now a discount, not a rule, and the agency managing that account needs to know that and re-implement the control properly.

## The Documented Workaround: Account-Level Brand Safety & Suitability Controls

The good news is that Meta has not removed every placement-blocking mechanism — it has removed the ad-set-level one. Account-level controls, found under Brand Safety & Suitability (previously called Brand Safety controls), still allow a genuine block, and — importantly — an account-level exclusion applies across every campaign in that ad account, including new campaigns built entirely through automated Advantage+ placement flows. It is also not subject to the 5%-leak or value-rule discount behaviour that ad-set-level settings have shown; ad-tech documentation of this mechanism describes it as the more durable of the two options precisely because it sits above the auction logic that value rules operate inside.

### Step-by-Step: Setting an Account-Level Placement Exclusion

1. Open Meta Ads Manager and go to Business Settings (or Brand Safety settings, depending on your account's current navigation — Meta has moved this menu more than once in 2026).
2. Find the Brand Safety & Suitability section, sometimes labelled Inventory Filter or Placement Controls at the account level.
3. Select the placement categories you want to block — Audience Network, specific content types, or category-level exclusions such as sensitive content tiers, depending on what your account offers.
4. Apply the setting at the ad account level, not inside an individual ad set. This is the critical step: an ad-set-level rule is a value rule with a discount; an account-level Brand Safety setting is closer to an actual filter on eligible inventory.
5. Confirm the setting applies to campaigns built under both manual and Advantage+ / unified flows — this is the specific gap that the February 2026 Advantage+ merge and the August 2026 checkbox removal opened, and the account-level control is the one surface documented to close it.
6. Re-check the setting after any major Meta interface update. Given the pattern above, treat this as a recurring quarterly task, not a one-time setup.

### Why This Belongs to Whoever Manages the Ad Account, Not Just the Client

Most business owners in Pune running Meta ads through an agency will never see this menu — it sits several clicks deep in account settings, not inside the campaign-creation flow most people interact with daily. That is exactly why it needs to be an explicit line item in whatever a digital marketing agency in Pune does for account hygiene, rather than something assumed to be "already handled." An agency that only checks ad-set-level settings, because that is what used to work, will not notice this gap exists.

## What a Competent Digital Marketing Agency in Pune Should Be Auditing This Quarter

Given the pace and quietness of these changes, here is a practical checklist that should be run against every active Meta ad account this quarter, not just once:

- **Audit every ad set that previously had placement exclusions set.** Confirm whether those exclusions are now showing as value rules, and document the bid-adjustment percentage currently applied.
- **Identify any client with a brand-safety, contractual, or compliance-driven reason for excluding a placement** (as opposed to a pure cost-efficiency reason), and treat those as priority accounts for migrating to account-level Brand Safety & Suitability settings.
- **Set the account-level exclusion once, and verify it persists** across campaign types, including new Advantage+ / unified campaigns created after February 2026.
- **Check Meta's release notes and ad-tech trade press monthly**, not just when something breaks. Given four changes in 19 months, a fifth narrowing of manual control before the end of 2026 would not be surprising, and catching it early avoids weeks of unnoticed budget drift.
- **Communicate the change to clients directly**, especially NGOs and regulated-adjacent businesses that specifically asked for placement exclusions in writing. Silence here is the biggest risk — a client who believes a placement is blocked, when it is merely discounted, is one uncomfortable audit away from a difficult conversation.

This kind of granular platform-change tracking is not a one-time task; it sits in the same category as the reporting changes Google made to Performance Max earlier in 2026 (see [our breakdown of those Performance Max reporting changes](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-performance-max-2026)) and Google's own reversal on third-party cookies (covered in [our article on Google's cookie U-turn and first-party data strategy](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-third-party-cookies-2026)). Ad platforms are moving faster and communicating less about the specifics, which raises the value of an agency whose actual job includes reading the trade press and re-auditing account settings, rather than treating campaign setup as a "set once" task.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Did Meta officially announce that placement exclusions were removed?

No. As of this writing, Meta has not published an official announcement specifically confirming the removal of ad-set-level placement exclusion checkboxes. What exists is a consistent pattern of reports from advertisers who noticed the checkboxes disappearing from their own accounts around 25 August 2026, documented independently by several ad-tech publications. It is accurate to describe this as "widely reported and documented" rather than as a confirmed Meta policy statement, and any digital marketing agency in Pune advising clients on this should be equally careful with that distinction.

### Can I still fully block a specific placement, like Facebook Audience Network, from showing my ads?

Not at the ad-set level anymore — that option has been replaced by value rules, which apply a bid discount (as steep as -90%) rather than a true block. You can still block a placement more reliably by using the account-level Brand Safety & Suitability settings in Business Settings, which apply across all campaigns in the account, including automated Advantage+ campaigns, and are not subject to the same discount-not-block behaviour.

### What happens to campaigns that already had placement exclusions set before this change?

Based on advertiser reports, existing ad-set-level exclusions were not deleted outright but were converted into value rules with a heavy negative bid adjustment on the previously excluded placement. In practice this means an exclusion set up months ago may now function as a steep discount rather than a hard block, without any change visible in the campaign name or obvious settings — which is exactly why an account audit is worth doing rather than assuming old settings still behave the way they did when you created them.

### Is this the same thing as the Advantage+ campaign changes from February 2026?

They are related but distinct. The February 2026 unified Advantage+ campaign structure prohibited placement exclusions at the campaign level as part of merging manual and Advantage+ campaign flows into one automated-by-default structure. The August 2026 change removed the separate, ad-set-level exclusion checkbox that had still existed underneath that structure. Together, the two changes mean manual placement exclusion no longer exists as a real option at either the campaign or the ad-set level — only the account-level Brand Safety & Suitability setting remains a genuine block.

### How do I actually set an account-level placement exclusion instead of an ad-set-level one?

In Meta Ads Manager, go to Business Settings and locate the Brand Safety & Suitability (or Inventory Filter / Placement Controls) section at the ad-account level, not inside an individual campaign or ad set. Select the placement categories or content types you want to exclude and apply the setting there. Because it sits at the account level, it applies across every campaign in that account — including ones built through fully automated Advantage+ placement flows — and it does not carry the same bid-discount behaviour that ad-set-level value rules do, which is why ad-tech sources currently document it as the more reliable option.

## Where to Go From Here

If you're running Meta campaigns for a business or NGO in Pune and you're not sure whether your account's placement settings still do what you think they do, that uncertainty is worth resolving before it turns into a brand-safety incident rather than after.
